key_insight: Molecular dynamics shows that in β-Sn, ⟨c⟩ dislocations can be absorbed by (301) twin boundaries and drive a faceting reaction whose facet length increases with each absorbed dislocation.
engineering_relevance: This mechanism helps explain how Sn-based solder microstructures may evolve under plastic loading, affecting twin-boundary stability, strength, and damage tolerance.
method: MD simulations of β-Sn twin-dislocation interactions
Machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP) for atomistic accuracy
evidence_signal: The authors compare simulated facet-length growth against isotropic elasticity theory and report agreement only when the asymmetric twin facet’s disclination character is included.
watch_item: The faceting prediction depends on atomistic simulations and a specific MLIP, so transferability to other loads, temperatures, or alloy chemistries may be limited.
paper_title: Dislocation mediated twin boundary faceting in $β$-Sn
